title: Rooftop Secret
source: Midnight Bet — Integrated ARC I — Old Friends, New Heat
paragraphs: Aarav’s day began with Ananya removing his excuses one by one. “Sit.” He sat. “Phone away.” He put it face-down. “Jacket?” He looked at her. “What about it?” “You keep adjusting it.” “The room is warm.” “Then remove it.” Aarav smiled. “Teacher privilege?” “Common sense.” He took the jacket off. Placed it over the chair. The white shirt underneath fitted close across his chest and shoulders. The fabric stretched when he moved.

Ananya’s eyes moved once. Shoulders. Arms. The line of his throat where the collar sat open. Then back to his face. Aarav caught it. Neither mentioned it. The knowledge sat between them like heat. “Mock interview.” She sat opposite. Closer than usual. Close enough that when she leaned forward to check her notes, the soft upper curves of her breasts pressed against the thin fabric of her blouse. “Question one.” Aarav answered.

Good. Too polished. Ananya tilted her head. “Again.” He sighed. “More honest.” He answered again. This time her eyes did not leave him. Aarav felt it — the weight of her gaze on his mouth, his throat, the open collar of his shirt. “Better.” “Because?” “You stopped performing.” He smiled.

“You like that version.” Ananya paused. “Professionally.” “Of course.” Aarav’s smile widened. She looked down at her notes. “Question two.” The word professionally hung between them as its own joke. At noon, Aarav left with no touch beyond a handshake. Still, he carried the session into the evening — the memory of her eyes on his body, the way she had watched him remove the jacket, the deliberate proximity of her chair.

The alumni cultural night was at the old college campus. Not school. Different building. Different age. Old friends. New bodies. Mira arrived in black. Not dramatic. Sleeveless midi dress that sat close to her body, showing the clean line of her collarbones, the soft swell of her breasts, the narrow waist and the curve of her hips. Light shrug open at the front. Aarav saw her from across the courtyard. Stopped walking.

His eyes moved over her the way Ananya’s had moved over him that morning — thorough, deliberate, impossible to hide. Naina saw him stop. “Good?” Aarav looked at her. “What?” “Mira.” He frowned. Naina laughed. “You are terrible.” Mira joined them. “Who is terrible?”

“Aarav.” “Known.” He looked at her. “You look…” Mira raised an eyebrow. “Continue.” Aarav remembered Ananya. Stop performing. “Good.” Mira blinked. Just once. “Good?” “Very.” Naina smiled. Mira recovered. “Dangerous honesty.” Aarav: “Trying something new.” Kabir arrived with Rhea. They were arguing before reaching the group.

“You drove like a criminal.” “You navigated like one.” Rhea wore dark jeans that hugged her hips and thighs, and a fitted top that sat close enough to show the soft shape of her breasts when she moved. Kabir had clearly noticed. He had also clearly decided not to show it — which only made the effort more obvious. Rhea enjoyed that. Dev arrived last. Naina looked at him. Dark shirt, sleeves rolled, the fabric fitted across his chest and the soft line of his forearms.

Dev caught her looking. “Problem?” She smiled. “You people really love that line.” The event moved through normal things. Music. Food stalls. Old faculty hellos. Alumni jokes. Yet every ordinary beat carried another layer. Mira watched Aarav talk to Sana — the way Sana’s body angled toward him, the way her hand rested near his arm. Aarav watched Mehul compliment Mira’s dress — the calm way Mehul’s eyes moved over the sleeveless black fabric, the soft upper curves of her breasts, the way the dress sat on her hips.

Rhea watched Kabir accept a glass from Tara — the brief contact of their fingers, the way Tara’s maroon sari draped over the soft curve of her body. Kabir watched Arjun lean toward Rhea while laughing — the proximity, the way Arjun’s eyes dropped once to the fitted top before returning to her face. Dev watched Naina dance with Mehul for thirty seconds — the way Mehul’s hand sat at her waist, the way her body moved under the short dress.

Naina watched Dev watching. Nobody belonged to anyone. Everyone noticed anyway. Tara and Rohan joined after dinner. Tara wore a deep maroon sari that sat low on her hips and left her midriff bare. The fabric clung to the soft curve of her breasts and the narrow line of her waist. Kabir looked once. Then again. Rhea caught both. Tara caught the second. She smiled. Rohan did not. Or maybe he did and said nothing. At the dance area, Sana pulled Aarav into a group circle.

Mira stayed outside. Mehul joined beside her. “You don’t dance?” “I do.” “Then?” Mira looked at Aarav. “Selective.” Mehul smiled. “Dangerous.” She turned. “Why does everyone say that?” “Maybe pattern.” He held out his hand. Mira looked. Then took it. One song. Group dance. Nothing private. Still, Mehul’s hand settled at the soft curve of her waist, fingers spanning the place where the black dress was thinnest. Warm. Steady. Different from Aarav’s reflex grab weeks ago.
Aarav’s face changed. Sana saw. She leaned toward him. Close enough that her breast brushed his arm through the fabric of her top. “You are not subtle.” Aarav: “I am fine.” “Of course.”

Meanwhile, Arjun stood near Rhea at the snack counter. Neha was talking to Tara. Arjun said: “White shirt was good.” Rhea turned. “You remember?” “Yes.” “Why?” He looked at her. “You know why.” Same phrase. Different man. Rhea’s pulse changed. Heat settled low in her stomach. Before she answered, Kabir appeared.

“Need anything?” Rhea looked at him. “No.” Kabir looked at Arjun. “Good.” He walked away. Rhea watched. Arjun smiled. “Jealous.” “Who?” “Both of you.” Rhea looked at him. “Careful.” He nodded. “Exactly.” The evening climbed toward rooftop fireworks. People moved upstairs. The roof was crowded at first. Then thinned. Mira stepped away from the group. Not because of Aarav. Because of noise. She stood near the far railing.

Wind. City lights. Her shrug still on, the sleeveless black dress moving against her body with the breeze. Aarav found her five minutes later. “Escaping?” “Breathing.” He stood beside her. Not too close. But close enough that she could feel the heat of his body and smell the faint scent of his cologne. Mira looked at him.

“You followed.” “Yes.” “Why?” Aarav thought of Ananya’s exercise. Honest. “Because you left.” Mira’s expression changed. “That simple?” “Yes.” She looked away. Downstairs music thumped. On the other side of the roof, Kabir and Rhea argued about photos. Dev and Naina disappeared toward the stairwell for water. Sana and Mehul stood with Tara and Rohan. Neha and Arjun were leaving. The roof still held people. Mira and Aarav felt alone anyway.

She asked: “You were jealous.” Aarav laughed softly. “Mehul?” “Maybe.” “Were you?” “Sana?” Mira’s mouth tightened. Aarav smiled. “Interesting.” “Do not enjoy it.” “Impossible.” Mira stepped closer. Not much. But enough that the soft side of her breast almost brushed his arm through the black dress. Enough that he could see the exact line of her collarbones and the soft shadow between her breasts.

“You looked at me like that this morning,” she said. “When?” “When I arrived. The same way Ananya looks at you.” Aarav went still. Mira smiled. “You thought I would not notice?” He did not answer. The silence between them thickened. Downstairs, fireworks began. Neither of them looked. They stayed at the railing, close enough to feel each other’s breath, the erotic current between them no longer possible to pretend was anything else.

“Tell me to move.” Mira inhaled. “I did not tell you to move.” The air changed. Aarav’s hands stayed at his sides. “Can I kiss you?” Mira should have remembered everything. The group. The pact jokes. The possibility of being seen. Sana downstairs. Mehul’s attention. Every reason to keep it theoretical. Instead:

“Yes.” Aarav stepped closer. The first kiss was careful. Too careful. Like both expected an alarm. Mira’s hand caught his shirt. Aarav pulled back. Eyes on her. “Okay?” Mira answered by kissing him again. Stronger. Still non-graphic. Still fully clothed. But no longer experimental. Aarav’s hands settled at her waist. He paused. Mira did not pull away. Her arms moved around his shoulders. They felt each other deliberately for the first time.

Not a catch. Not a dance position. Not accident. Choice. Mira’s pulse raced. Aarav’s breathing changed. Then footsteps. Both separated. Fast. Rhea appeared at the rooftop door. Stopped. She saw distance. She did not see the kiss. Maybe. “Mira?” “Yeah.” “Leaving in ten.” Rhea looked between them. Aarav’s hair. Mira’s face. She knew something. Not enough. Rhea left. Mira looked at Aarav. The heat became fear. Aarav whispered:

“The group.” Mira’s face changed. “What?” He immediately knew he had said it badly. “I mean…” “The whole no-dating disaster.” Mira stepped back. “Right.” “No.” “Mira.” She fixed her shrug. “We should go.” Aarav reached. Stopped before touching. “Mira.” She looked at him.

“What?” He wanted to say: I did not regret that. He said: “This is complicated.” Wrong. Mira laughed without humour. “Good to know.” She walked away. Aarav stood alone. Ananya’s voice came back. Stop performing. Too late. Downstairs, Mira found Mehul by the exit. He looked at her.

“You okay?” “Fine.” Mehul held the door. Mira walked through. Aarav saw from across the lobby. Jealousy returned. Now mixed with panic. Kabir’s night carried a different secret. At the parking area, Tara struggled with a box from the event. Kabir took it. “Bhabhi.”

“I can carry.” “I know.” He held it anyway. Rohan had gone to bring the car. Tara stood beside Kabir. Wind lifted one edge of her sari pallu. She adjusted. Kabir looked away. Tara smiled. “You are very disciplined tonight.” “Trying.” “Why?” Kabir looked at her.

“Because you notice when I am not.” Tara went quiet. Rhea saw them from twenty feet away. Not words. Only posture. Kabir and Tara too close beside one box. Rhea’s jaw tightened. Arjun was walking beside her. He noticed. “Jealous?” Rhea looked at him. “Everyone asks that.”

“Maybe answer.” She looked back at Kabir. Then at Arjun. “Maybe.” Arjun smiled. The answer felt dangerous in two directions. Dev and Naina ended the night in a cab. Only them. Mira and Rhea had left together. Kabir drove Tara and Rohan. Aarav stayed behind pretending to help. Naina sat beside Dev. Their knees touched. Same as before. This time she did not pretend.

“Move?” Dev looked. “You want me to?” “No.” So he did not. Naina smiled. “Good.” Dev looked out the window. Shalini’s lesson came back. Stop retreating. He did. Neither touched beyond knees. It still felt like a decision. By midnight, one secret kiss existed. Three near-secrets had deepened. Aarav lay awake replaying Mira. Mira lay awake replaying the word complicated. Kabir replayed Tara asking why he was disciplined.
Rhea replayed her own maybe. Dev replayed Naina’s knee. Naina replayed his refusal to move away. The world remained ordinary. The baseline did not
One secret kiss now existed. The next ordinary accident would have to compete with the fact that at least two people already knew what choosing felt like..
